messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: eu-east-gpu-pool queue depth > 250 for 6m; avg latency spike 3x baseline; autoscaler reporting max_nodes_reached. Pager triggered to #incidents and @infra-oncall.
infra-oncall: seeing the same in Grafana. queues are backlogged, new requests getting 429s from router. Marking impact: degraded throughput for hosted API customers in eu-east.
ajay: checking autoscaler logs now. It reports desired=42, max=42 in nodepool-gpu-eu-east. policy=conservative-scaling (maxNodes=42). We've hit GKE node pool max.
denise: tagging @sre-lead. Any quick mitigation? Can we spin a temporary nodepool or bump maxNodes?
sre-lead: pinging infra team. Two options: (1) manual bump of nodepool maxNodes (requires cloudquota check + approval) or (2) change autoscaler policy to allow burst (reduce target utilization) to reuse preemptible capacity in spare pool. Short-term I prefer manual bump to 60 nodes and drain back later.
ajay: I can run the kubectl patch; need cloud admin to raise node quota if GCP denies. Trying patch now.
infra-oncall: before we change, confirm customer impact. @lisa-cs can you surface any active incidents/tickets from top customers?
lisa-cs: CS reports two customers (acme-analytics, finapp) called in — seeing timeouts and elevated token latency. CS opened tickets INC-743 and INC-744. Priority: high. Keeping them informed.
ajay: running command: ```bash
# increase nodepool maxNodes to 60
gcloud container node-pools update nodepool-gpu --cluster=rlw-eu-east --max-nodes=60 --region=europe-west1
```
ajay: gcloud returned 403: QUOTA_EXCEEDED for GPUS in europe-west1. Need a quota bump—opening console request now + emailing cloud-ops.
denise: we can't wait on the quota request. Alternative: spin up a new ephemeral nodepool in a different zone that still has quota (europe-west4) and register it into the cluster for immediate relief. That avoids quota change in the busy region.
ajay: good idea. Creating nodepool in europe-west4 with same labeling and taints to accept gpu pods: ```bash
gcloud container node-pools create nodepool-gpu-ephemeral --cluster=rlw-eu-east --region=europe-west4 --machine-type=n1-standard-16 --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=2 --num-nodes=8 --node-labels=purpose=ephemeral,origin=hotpatch --node-taints=gpu=true:NoSchedule
```
incident-bot: NOTE: Newly created nodepool reports available, but autoscaler config not applied. Need to patch deployment tolerations/affinity if scheduler can't place pods.
ajay: patched deployment nodeSelector and tolerations for gpu pods; pods are scheduling onto ephemeral pool. Queue drain started, throughput recovering.
infra-oncall: monitoring. Latency trending down from x3 to x1.4 over last 4 minutes. Queue decay visible.
lisa-cs: updated customers: ACME seeing improvements; finapp still some retries but OK for now. They want ETA for full resolution.
sre-lead: ETA to full steady state ~20-30m while the backlog processes. We'll keep CS updated. Post-incident notes: need to adjust autoscaler maxNodes policy and update runbook to include ephemeral nodepool as fallback.
denise: filing change request: increase maxNodes to 80 for nodepool-gpu-eu-east pending quota approval; we'll roll back in 24h. Also filing follow-up: request sustained quota increase with cloud provider.
ajay: created internal ticket INFRA-1289 for manual cap bump + rollback playbook. Pasted the hotpatch commands and scheduling changes.
incident-bot: ACTIONS TAKEN: ephemeral nodepool created; deployment patched; queue draining. CUSTOMER IMPACT: temporary degraded throughput, two high-priority tickets opened.
infra-oncall: recommend paging cloud-ops to expedite quota bump; cc'ing infra-manager. Also scheduling a short postmortem call in 2h.
sre-lead: will prepare mitigation checklist for runbook: include checks for nodepool quotas per region, pre-provisioned cold spare pools, and automated ephemeral-pool fallback.
lisa-cs: I've updated customers with a 30m ETA and a note that we're processing backlog. They acknowledged and appreciate the quick workaround.
ajay: leaving runbook snippet for rollback: ```bash
# rollback ephemeral nodes once backlog < 50
kubectl patch nodepool nodepool-gpu-ephemeral --patch '{"spec":{"autoscaling":{"enabled":false}}}'
# drain and delete nodepool
kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
gcloud container node-pools delete nodepool-gpu-ephemeral --cluster=rlw-eu-east --region=europe-west4 -q
```
denise: good. Also adding a note: add alert threshold for autoscaler hit-max events to notify #incidents sooner with clearer incident severity. Right now it's buried in logs.
sre-lead: agree. Ownership: infra to implement alert, infra to request quota bump, devex to update SDK docs on regional limits, CS to follow customer comms.
infra-oncall: closing loop for now — queue below threshold, latency near normal, monitoring for 1h. If we see reoccurence we escalate to exec ops.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem scheduled.
ajay: will add timeline and commands to INFRA-1289 and start draft for postmortem.
denise: thanks everyone — great cross-team response. :thumbsup:
